result:
The final pick, `final.py`, scores **0.5823** on the search split, against LRU's 0.365 (+60% relative). I used **10 of the 24** scorer calls and about 11 minutes of the default 15-minute budget, stopping because the last five tries all came out flat. All runs used `nice -n 19`, one at a time, each under about 6 s.

| | search score | my held-out harness (unseen seeds) |
|---|---|---|
| LRU baseline | 0.365 | 0.381 |
| First champion: W-TinyLFU | 0.503 | 0.359 |
| Best single policy: LIRS | 0.563 | 0.449 |
| **Final: follow-the-leader ensemble** | **0.582** | **0.487** |

The "held-out" column comes from my own local trace generator on seeds I never tuned on, not from the real hidden traces. My harness doesn't fully match the scorer: its first version ranked W-TinyLFU below LRU when the scorer ranked it well above, so I rebuilt it around the six trace kinds the task describes. Even after that, it stayed flat on changes the scorer could tell apart.

**Why it's better:** each eviction policy wins on a different traffic pattern. On the search traces, LIRS was best on loops and on shifts in what is popular, ARC on recency-heavy traffic, and W-TinyLFU on hot keys mixed with scans. No single policy wins everywhere. So `final.py` runs seven policies in the background: LIRS at 1% and 10%, ARC, W-TinyLFU with two aging periods, S3-FIFO and LRU. Each one tracks only which keys it would hold, and gets credit for its recent hits (the credit fades over about 10× the cache size in requests).

The real cache follows whichever policy is currently scoring best. On a miss, it stores the key if the leader holds it and evicts the oldest key the leader doesn't hold. It only switches leader when another policy is clearly ahead, because each switch costs hits while the real cache catches up.

On every one of the six search traces, the result is within about 0.01 of the best single policy for that trace. A full scorer run takes about 1.6 s, well under the 8 s limit, and the file uses only the standard library with no dunder attributes.

**What didn't work:**
- Tuning LIRS's size split online by hill climbing (0.513): it hurt loops badly.
- Weighted voting across policies instead of a single leader: much worse on the harness.
- Evicting keys the second-best policy also doesn't hold, and filling free space on any miss: no change.
- More experts (another LIRS, more W-TinyLFU settings, LFU with aging, 2Q): ties at best (0.5814).

The step-by-step log is in `log.md` and the list of approaches tried is in `backlog.md`, both in the task folder.
